info.title: Wizer Signage API
info.description: Wizer Signage — multi-tenant digital signage SaaS platform REST API.

status.description: Always `ok`; the process answering at all IS the check.

version.description: The API version, read from package.json at startup.

mailConfigured.description: An SMTP transport is configured; otherwise mail is log-only.

status.description: Under a 200 this is always `ok`; `degraded` arrives with a 503.

companyName.description: The tenant slug is derived from this; the allocated slug may differ if it collides.

password.description: The owner account password. `PasswordService.evaluate()` runs on it in public.service.ts, so the full policy applies — upper, lower, digit, symbol, and no common/breached password — not merely the 10-character minimum this validator states.

captchaToken.description: ACCEPTED AND IGNORED — no provider is wired up and nothing in the codebase reads this field, so a token buys no bot protection. The actual protection on this route is the rate limit (5/hour per IP).

slug.description: The tenant slug, as allocated — may differ from what was asked for.

redirectUrl.description: Where to send the browser next. NO tokens are issued here — the owner signs in normally, so an unauthenticated endpoint never mints a session.

captchaToken.description: ACCEPTED AND IGNORED. Nothing in the codebase reads this field — it is a placeholder for a captcha that is not wired up, so sending a token buys no bot protection and omitting one costs nothing. Documented rather than hidden, because a field named captchaToken otherwise implies a verification step that does not happen. Rate limiting (5/hour per IP) is the actual protection on this route.

priceMonthly.description: The raw Decimal as a string, matching GET /plans and every other money field. Parse it before doing arithmetic; do not assume a JS number round-trips it exactly.

priceYearly.description: A string, or null when the plan is not sold yearly.

limits.description: `{}` when the plan sets no limits.

actorId.description: Nulled if the actor is deleted.

category.description: A plain String column, not an enum.

token.description: The single-use token from the confirmation link. Consumed on first use; requesting a new link invalidates any outstanding one.

success.description: Always true; failures are returned as errors.

email.description: The address that is now confirmed.
Always answered identically whether or not the address exists or is already verified — this route is unauthenticated and a truthful answer would make it an account-existence oracle.

success.description: Fixed acknowledgement. Does NOT indicate that an email was sent — see the oracle note on the request shape.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier, unique across the platform.

The tenant identifier used in URLs. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only. Derived from the name when omitted, and the allocated value may differ from what was asked for if it collides. CREATE-ONLY — there is no field for it on update.

timezone.description: IANA zone name. Length-checked only, not validated against the tz database.

planId.description: Starts a TRIALING subscription on this plan. CREATE-ONLY: changing plan later goes through the subscriptions endpoints, not through a company update.

primaryColor.description: Free-form, capped at 20 characters and NOT pattern-checked — unlike `CreateTagDto.color`, which demands a hex value. Same kind of field, two different rules; anything short enough is accepted here.

defaultKioskPin.description: Plaintext 4-8 digit PIN. Hashed on receipt and never returned — responses expose only `hasDefaultKioskPin`, so this cannot be read back.

pendingInvitations.description: Non-expired PENDING invitations. Counted because each one RESERVES a user seat — a company at its user limit with outstanding invitations is already full.

storageBytes.description: A string, matching the per-row `fileSize` it sums — that field is a 64-bit column and has always serialised as a string. This aggregate used to go through Number(), making the same quantity two types depending on which endpoint you asked.

limit.description: null means unlimited on this plan.

approaching.description: At or above 80% of the limit, and not yet exceeded.

percentUsed.description: null when unlimited, or when the limit is zero.

status.description: Worst status across every metered resource. `grace` and `blocked` are both over-limit states — the difference is whether the grace window has run out.

graceExpired.description: A grace window existed and has passed.

subscriptionStatus.description: Copied through as a plain string, not the SubscriptionStatus enum.

primaryColor.description: Not pattern-checked — see the create DTO.

brandedEmailFrom.description: UPDATE-ONLY — cannot be supplied at creation.

customDomain.description: UPDATE-ONLY — cannot be supplied at creation.

defaultKioskPin.description: Plaintext 4-8 digit PIN. Hashed on receipt and never returned — responses expose only `hasDefaultKioskPin`, so this cannot be read back.

reason.description: Recorded on the company and in the activity log. Optional — a suspension with no stated reason is accepted, so the body itself may be empty.

impersonatorId.description: Set only on a Super Admin impersonation session. The real human at the keyboard; `userId` is the impersonated principal.

refreshRotatedAt.description: When the refresh token was last rotated. Bounds the grace window.

revokedAt.description: Always null here — the endpoint only returns sessions that are still live.

current.description: True for the session making the request — added by the view, not a column. This is how a client knows which row NOT to offer a sign-out button for.

revokedCount.description: Number of sessions revoked. Renamed from `revoked`.

revoked.description: Always true. The bulk routes return revokedCount.

companyId.description: null for a platform-level Super Admin.

role.description: Granting or removing SUPER_ADMIN requires the caller to BE a Super Admin, and demoting the last active one is refused outright — both enforced in the service, not here.

status.description: Setting a status other than ACTIVE goes through the same authority check as a role change, so this is not a back door to disabling an account you could not demote.

twoFactorEnforced.description: Makes 2FA mandatory for this user, as it always is for a Super Admin.

locationIds.description: REPLACES the assigned set — it does not add to it. Sending one id leaves the user with exactly that location, and `[]` removes every assignment. Omit the field to leave the current set alone; the two are NOT the same thing.

required.description: Whether 2FA is mandatory for this account.

password.description: The signed-in user's own password. Required on every route in this module — a bearer token alone no longer authorises changing the second factor.

currentCode.description: A TOTP or backup code from the authenticator currently enrolled. REQUIRED when the account already has 2FA on, and rejected as missing if omitted then; ignored otherwise. Optional in the schema because whether it is needed depends on account state, not shape.

secret.description: Base32 TOTP secret, in plaintext, for manual entry. A credential: anyone holding it can generate valid codes. Returned only during enrollment and never readable afterwards.

otpauthUrl.description: otpauth:// URI. Contains the same secret — treat it with the same care.

qrCodeDataUrl.description: The otpauth URI rendered as a QR code, inline as a data: URL. Same secret again.

password.description: The signed-in user's own password. Required on every route in this module — a bearer token alone no longer authorises changing the second factor.

currentCode.description: A TOTP or backup code from the authenticator currently enrolled. REQUIRED when the account already has 2FA on, and rejected as missing if omitted then; ignored otherwise. Optional in the schema because whether it is needed depends on account state, not shape.

code.description: A 6-digit code from the NEW authenticator, checked against the pending secret. Distinct from `currentCode`, which comes from the old one.

backupCodes.description: Single-use recovery codes, shown once and never retrievable. Each is consumed on use.

password.description: The signed-in user's own password. Required on every route in this module — a bearer token alone no longer authorises changing the second factor.

currentCode.description: A TOTP or backup code from the authenticator currently enrolled. REQUIRED when the account already has 2FA on, and rejected as missing if omitted then; ignored otherwise. Optional in the schema because whether it is needed depends on account state, not shape.

code.description: A 6-digit TOTP code or a formatted backup code (e.g. ABCD-EFGH), proving possession of the factor being removed. Send `password` as well; `currentCode` is not needed here because this field already is the current code.

role.description: Required — an invitation always carries a role. As on user update, the enum is wider than any one caller may use: inviting a SUPER_ADMIN requires being one.

companyId.description: SUPER ADMIN ONLY, and the one field here that crosses a tenant boundary. For everyone else the company comes from the token and this is ignored — it is never trusted as the caller-supplied tenant (see docs/multi-tenancy.md).

locationIds.description: Scopes a LOCATION_MANAGER to these locations. Meaningless for other roles, and not rejected for them — it is simply unused.

companyId.description: null for a platform-level Super Admin.

token.description: Single-use acceptance token, returned ONLY here. The database stores a hash, so it cannot be read back later. Treat it as a credential: do not log it, and deliver it over a channel you would send a password reset link over.

companyId.description: null for a platform-level Super Admin.

accessToken.description: Short-lived bearer token for the Authorization header.

mustEnableTwoFactor.description: True when the account must enrol in 2FA before it has full access — a Super Admin, or a user whose company enforces it. The session is confined to the enrollment routes until it does.

challengeToken.description: Present the code for this challenge at POST /auth/login/2fa.

password.description: Deliberately carries NO minimum length and NO policy. Sign-in must be able to ATTEMPT any password, including one set before the policy existed; imposing the rule here would lock those accounts out of their own account, surfacing as "invalid credentials" for a password that is correct. The cap is a DoS bound — Argon2 verification is expensive.

challengeToken.description: The short-lived token returned by POST /auth/login when the account has 2FA. It is NOT an access token and carries no authority of its own; it is single-use and tied to a server-side challenge record.

code.description: A 6-digit TOTP code OR a formatted backup code (e.g. ABCD-EFGH) — hence the 6..12 range rather than a 6-digit pattern.

email.description: The response is identical whether or not this address exists, so it cannot be used to enumerate accounts. A 200 here does not mean an email was sent.

token.description: The single-use token from the reset email. Expires one hour after issue.

password.description: At least 10 characters, including an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a symbol. Also rejected: passwords on the common/breached list, and reusing your current password. Enforced server-side by PasswordService, so the length below is the floor, not the whole rule.

token.description: The single-use token from the invitation email. Expires three days after issue.

password.description: At least 10 characters, including an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a symbol. Also rejected: passwords on the common/breached list, and reusing your current password. Enforced server-side by PasswordService, so the length below is the floor, not the whole rule.

email.description: Taken from the invitation, never from the request body.

permissions.description: Effective permissions, derived from the DATABASE role rather than the token.

twoFactorRequired.description: Whether 2FA is mandatory for this account.

maxCompanies.description: Max child companies. Reseller-readiness — not enforced in v1. Null or omitted means unlimited.

maxLocations.description: Max locations (branches). Null or omitted means unlimited.

maxScreens.description: Max paired screens. Null or omitted means unlimited.

maxUsers.description: Max user accounts in the company. Null or omitted means unlimited.

storageGb.description: Content storage cap, in gigabytes. Null or omitted means unlimited.

maxFileSizeMb.description: Largest single upload, in megabytes. Null or omitted means unlimited.

autoScreenshotsPerDay.description: Automatic screenshots per screen per day. Null or omitted means unlimited.

scheduledReports.description: Max scheduled report definitions. Null or omitted means unlimited.

dataRetentionDays.description: Per-plan override of the retention window, in days. Null or omitted means unlimited.

apiRequestsPerDay.description: Future-ready. Not enforced in v1. Null or omitted means unlimited.

webhooks.description: Future-ready. Not enforced in v1. Null or omitted means unlimited.

code.description: Stable machine code, unique across plans. Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens.

priceMonthly.description: RENAMED from `price`, which is what the response has always called it — a plan could not be round-tripped by copying fields. Sent as a NUMBER (two decimal places) and returned as a string, because the column is a Decimal: that asymmetry is deliberate, since a JSON request body has no decimal type to send.

priceYearly.description: A number in, a string out — same reason as priceMonthly.

currency.description: Exactly three characters. Not checked against ISO 4217 — "XXX" is accepted.

isActive.description: Inactive plans cannot take new subscriptions.

isPublic.description: Whether it appears on the public pricing endpoint.

limits.description: Per-plan quotas. `{}` means the plan sets no limits, which reads as UNLIMITED rather than zero.

priceMonthly.description: Decimal(12,2) — a STRING on the wire. Trailing zeros are not preserved.

priceYearly.description: Decimal(12,2) as a string. null when the plan is not sold yearly.

trialDays.description: Length of the trial a new subscription gets. 0 for none.

isActive.description: An inactive plan is hidden but keeps its subscriptions.

isPublic.description: Whether the plan is offered publicly.

limits.description: The same limit block GET /companies/{id}/usage evaluates against. Absent or null on a field means UNLIMITED, not zero.

priceMonthly.description: RENAMED from `price`, which is what the response has always called it — a plan could not be round-tripped by copying fields. Sent as a NUMBER (two decimal places) and returned as a string, because the column is a Decimal: that asymmetry is deliberate, since a JSON request body has no decimal type to send.

trialDays.description: Converted to a trialEndsAt date, and ONLY when status is TRIALING — sending it with any other status has no effect and is not rejected.

gracePeriodEndsAt.description: Set when an over-limit account is given time to come back under.

cancelAtPeriodEnd.description: Cancel at the end of the paid period rather than immediately.

gracePeriodEndsAt.description: Set when an over-limit account is given time to come back under.

cancelAtPeriodEnd.description: Cancel at the end of the paid period rather than immediately.

planId.description: Moves the tenant to another plan.

trialEndsAt.description: A DATE here, where create takes `trialDays`, a count.

cancelAtPeriodEnd.description: Ends the subscription at period end rather than now.

unitPrice.description: Two decimal places. Sent as a NUMBER; invoice money comes BACK as a string, because responses carry the raw Prisma Decimal.

companyId.description: The tenant billed. A Super Admin route, so it is named in the body.

subscriptionId.description: Links the invoice to a subscription, if it belongs to one.

lineItems.description: At least one line — an empty invoice is refused. Totals are computed server-side.

tax.description: An absolute AMOUNT, not a percentage or rate.

subscriptionId.description: Nulled rather than cascaded if the subscription goes away.

tax.description: Decimal(12,2) as a string. null when no tax applies.

lineItems.description: Free-form JSON line items; nothing in the schema constrains their shape.

status.description: Status is the ONLY mutable field — line items and amounts cannot be edited after issue, and financial records are never deleted by the retention sweep.

twoFactorCode.description: A current TOTP or single-use backup code. Impersonation is re-authenticated even though the caller already holds a Super Admin session — entering a tenant is not something a stolen token should be able to do.

reason.description: REQUIRED, minimum 10 characters — deliberately long enough to be a sentence. "test" is not a reason, and a field that accepts it produces an audit trail nobody trusts. Written to the activity log alongside the impersonation.

accessToken.description: Short-lived bearer token scoped to the impersonated company.

reason.description: The justification the admin gave when starting it (`impersonationNote`).

ip.description: Where the impersonation was started from.

byStatus.description: Every status in the enum, INCLUDING the ones at zero — `toStatusMap` seeds the map from the full enum before folding the groupBy in, so a missing key means a new status the API does not know about rather than a count of none.

unpaidTotal.description: A string, like the per-invoice `total` it sums. It used to be summed with Number(), making this the one money value in the API that was a JSON number.

active.description: Still TRIALING and not past its end date.

expired.description: EXPIRED, or TRIALING but past its end date — the second case is a subscription the expiry job has not swept yet, and it counts as expired here rather than as active.

email.description: Invites a PLATFORM administrator with cross-tenant access, not a company user. 2FA is mandatory for the resulting account and cannot be turned off.

status.description: The only field — a demo request is a pipeline record, and status is all that moves.

closed.description: When true, open/close are ignored and the day is outside hours.

open.description: 24h HH:mm. Omitted together with `close` means all-day open.

close.description: 24h HH:mm. OVERNIGHT IS ALLOWED — a close earlier than open crosses midnight.

timezone.description: IANA zone. Defaults to the entity's own timezone when omitted.

days.description: At most one entry per weekday. An ABSENT day counts as outside hours, so a partial array is not the same as an unset one: omitting `days` entirely means always on (24/7).

outsideHoursBehavior.description: Defaults to FALLBACK when omitted or unrecognised. The legacy values "SLEEP" and "BLANK_SCREEN" are both still ACCEPTED and treated as BLACK_SCREEN; neither is listed here because neither should be sent by new callers. They rendered black anyway — SLEEP never slept the display, and BLANK_SCREEN was an exact duplicate of BLACK_SCREEN.

outsideHoursMessage.description: Shown on the screen only when outsideHoursBehavior is CUSTOM_MESSAGE.

code.description: Your own reference for the branch. Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores only — no spaces and no dots, which rules out most codes copied out of a spreadsheet.

latitude.description: Decimal degrees. Independent of longitude — neither requires the other.

timezone.description: IANA zone name. Only length-checked here, NOT validated against the tz database — an unrecognised value is stored and surfaces later as wrong scheduling times, not as a 400.

status.description: A NARROWER set than the LocationStatus enum the API returns: ARCHIVED cannot be set here, because archived locations are exempt from the plan quota and creating one already archived would mint free capacity. Settable only at creation — it is omitted from the update body entirely, so this field cannot be used to archive later either.

companyId.description: Owning tenant. Derived from the caller's token, never the body.

timezone.description: IANA zone. Schedules resolve against it, so a bare city name runs them hours off.
